product_summary: A meeting intelligence product that turns conversations into organizational memory and execution workflows.
assumptions: The product integrates with calendar, CRM, and project systems.
Meeting history and customer-specific context compound over time.
The product owns post-meeting follow-up, not transcription alone.

dimensions.reason: Transcription and summarization can become native, but the surrounding workflow remains valuable.
Better models improve extraction, search, and follow-up quality.
Historical meeting context and organizational memory compound with use.
The product connects meetings to tasks, CRM records, and follow-up.
Core AI functions are reproducible, while integrations and accumulated context are harder to copy.
More AI-generated communication increases the need to capture decisions, ownership, and follow-through.
The reasoning model can be swapped without destroying the workflow or stored organizational context.
The product can evolve from a meeting utility into an execution and decision system of record.

why: The native meeting-summary layer is vulnerable to absorption.
Organizational memory and workflow integrations create durable value beyond the model.
The product becomes stronger if it owns execution after the meeting rather than only the meeting artifact.
best_modification: Own the post-meeting execution loop: commitments, approvals, CRM updates, accountability, and follow-up.
decisive_question: If transcription and summarization become free native features, does the product still own a workflow customers cannot easily replace?
